Pitch

Initial Context & Idea

  • Goal: Improve the checkout design, improve the checkout process → access 
  • Foundation: Create a compact checkout design so that all payment buttons are always visible, especially on small screens

Final Context & Idea

We are encountering a situation where the payment buttons on the checkout page do not fit within the viewport. Presumably, this could affect the number of people who use these buttons and, ultimately, the number of transactions a user could potentially make using these payment methods:

Reach & Impact

AVG Daily MetricsABdiff




Hypothesis

If we make the checkout page more compact and ensure that all payment buttons are clearly visible, we will increase conversion rates by 3% percent, because the people who use these buttons will be able to use them

    • reduce the spacing between the blocks

    • In the C test branch, we move the payment buttons above the card details

Results

#7328  – 

Exposure event: App Experiment Start

Decision GreenSUCCESS

  • The compact checkout with alternative payment methods placed above the credit card form delivered the strongest monetization results across the experiment
  • Winning variation showed the highest uplift in revenue metrics: access conversion, charge conversion, Trial → Charge conversion and ARPU, ARPU increased by +15.3% in variation 3
  • The main driver of revenue growth was a +28.4% uplift in Trial → Charge conversion, resulting in an estimated +$2.2K revenue uplift per day versus control
  • Moving alternative payment methods higher significantly changed payment behavior: credit cards share dropped from 68.3% to 55.7%, while PayPal usage increased from 12% to 18.7%
  • At the same time, there has been an increase in charge, which is particularly noticeable in the case of credit cards
    • here's an idea: encourage even more users to switch to payment buttons by hiding the credit card form behind the button
  • Rollout group 3 but monitor Charge → Cancel conversion

Significance analysis

  • Both test groups show an uplift in monetization metrics: access conversion, charge conversion, Trial → Charge and ARPU. For variation 2, none of the differences are statistically significant; for variation 3, the signal is stronger.
  • ARPU in variation 3 increased by +15.3%, and statistically signifficant, p = 0.024.
  • The main contributor to the Revenue lift is a +28.4% increase in Trial → Charge (p = 0.008).
  • However, significant negative effects in variation 3 are observed downstream of the charge:
    • The 14-day post-charge cancellation rate increased from 10% to 16.8% (+31.7%, p = 0.043);
    • 7-day retention dropped by −7.2% (p = 0.021), and 14-day retention by −6.5% (p = 0.023).
  • This indicates that the new checkout converts paid subscriptions more effectively, but the resulting subscribers are more likely to cancel after the first charge and show worse retention on the platform.

Pitch

Initial Context & Idea

  • Goal: Improve the checkout design, improve the checkout process → access 
  • Foundation: Create a compact checkout design so that all payment buttons are always visible, especially on small screens

Final Context & Idea

We are encountering a situation where the payment buttons on the checkout page do not fit within the viewport. Presumably, this could affect the number of people who use these buttons and, ultimately, the number of transactions a user could potentially make using these payment methods:

Reach & Impact

Hypothesis

If we make the checkout page more compact and ensure that all payment buttons are clearly visible, we will increase conversion rates by 3% percent, because the people who use these buttons will be able to use them

Results

#7328 04 May 2026  –  11 May 2026

Exposure event: App Experiment Start

Decision SUCCESS

  • The compact checkout with alternative payment methods placed above the credit card form delivered the strongest monetization results across the experiment
  • Winning variation showed the highest uplift in revenue metrics: access conversion, charge conversion, Trial → Charge conversion and ARPU, ARPU increased by +15.3% in variation 3
  • The main driver of revenue growth was a +28.4% uplift in Trial → Charge conversion, resulting in an estimated +$2.2K revenue uplift per day versus control
  • Moving alternative payment methods higher significantly changed payment behavior: credit cards share dropped from 68.3% to 55.7%, while PayPal usage increased from 12% to 18.7%
  • At the same time, there has been an increase in charge, which is particularly noticeable in the case of credit cards
    • here's an idea: encourage even more users to switch to payment buttons by hiding the credit card form behind the button
  • Rollout group 3 but monitor Charge → Cancel conversion

Significance analysis

  • Both test groups show an uplift in monetization metrics: access conversion, charge conversion, Trial → Charge and ARPU. For variation 2, none of the differences are statistically significant; for variation 3, the signal is stronger.
  • ARPU in variation 3 increased by +15.3%, and statistically signifficant, p = 0.024.
  • The main contributor to the Revenue lift is a +28.4% increase in Trial → Charge (p = 0.008).
  • However, significant negative effects in variation 3 are observed downstream of the charge:
    • The 14-day post-charge cancellation rate increased from 10% to 16.8% (+31.7%, p = 0.043);
    • 7-day retention dropped by −7.2% (p = 0.021), and 14-day retention by −6.5% (p = 0.023).
  • This indicates that the new checkout converts paid subscriptions more effectively, but the resulting subscribers are more likely to cancel after the first charge and show worse retention on the platform.

with exp_data as (
    select distinct
        id, name,
        toDateTime(date_start) as datetime_start,
        toDateTime(date_end) as datetime_end
    from default.ab_experiments as e
    where id = 7328
        and name like '%[UG Monetization]%'
)
, exp_users as (
    select 
        experiments.variation[indexOf(rt.experiments.id, 7328)] as variation,
        rt.unified_id as unified_id,
        argMin(user_id > 0, datetime) AS is_auth,
        min(rt.datetime) as exp_start_datetime,
        min(e.datetime_end) as exp_end_datetime
    from default.ug_rt_events_web rt
    left join exp_data e 
        on rt.item_id = e.id
    where rt.date between '2026-05-04' and '2026-05-11'
        and rt.event in ('App Experiment Start')
        and has(rt.experiments.id, 7328)
        and rt.item_id = 7328
        and rt.unified_id <> 0
        and rt.platform = 1
        and rt.datetime between e.datetime_start and if(toDate(e.datetime_end) = '1970-01-01', toDateTime('2029-01-01'), e.datetime_end)
    group by 1, 2
)
, subscribed as (
    select
        s.subscription_id as subscription_id,
        s.product_code as product_code,
        max(s.trial > 0) as is_trial,
        max(s.unified_id) as unified_id,
        min(s.datetime) as subscribed_dt,
        min(s.date) as subscribed_date
    from default.ug_subscriptions_events s
    inner join exp_users e
        on s.unified_id = e.unified_id
    where s.date between '2026-05-04' and '2026-05-11'
        and s.platform like '%WEB%'
        and s.event = 'Subscribed'
        and s.datetime between e.exp_start_datetime and if(toDate(e.exp_end_datetime) = '1970-01-01', toDateTime('2029-01-01'), e.exp_end_datetime)
        and lower(funnel_source) not like '%email%'
    group by 1, 2
)
, charged as (
    select
        subscription_id,
        product_code,
        min(case
            when product_id = 'com.ultimateguitar.tabs.one.intro.1year2' then 39.99
            when product_id like '%.intro.%' and billing_cycle = 1 then usd_price * 0.5
            else usd_price
        end) as charged_revenue,
        min(datetime) as charged_dt
    from default.ug_subscriptions_events
    where date >= '2026-05-04'
        and platform like '%WEB%'
        and event = 'Charged'
    group by 1, 2
)
, refunded as (
    select
        subscription_id,
        product_code,
        min(case
            when product_id = 'com.ultimateguitar.tabs.one.intro.1year2' then 39.99
            when product_id like '%.intro.%' and billing_cycle = 1 then usd_price * 0.5
            else usd_price
        end) as refunded_revenue,
        min(datetime) as refunded_dt
    from default.ug_subscriptions_events
    where date >= '2026-05-04'
        and platform like '%WEB%'
        and event = 'Refunded'
    group by 1, 2
)
, canceled as (
    select
        subscription_id,
        product_code,
        min(datetime) as canceled_dt
    from default.ug_subscriptions_events
    where date >= '2026-05-04'
        and platform like '%WEB%'
        and event = 'Canceled'
    group by 1, 2
)
, sub as (   
    select
        sub.unified_id as unified_id,
        sub.is_trial as is_trial,
        uniqExact(sub.subscription_id || sub.product_code) as accesses,
        uniqExactIf(sub.subscription_id || sub.product_code, sub.subscription_id = ch.subscription_id) as charges,
        sumIf(ch.charged_revenue, sub.subscription_id = ch.subscription_id) as charged_revenue,
        uniqExactIf(sub.subscription_id || sub.product_code, sub.subscription_id = r.subscription_id and sub.subscription_id = ch.subscription_id and dateDiff('day', charged_dt, refunded_dt) between 0 and 14) as refunds,
        sumIf(r.refunded_revenue, sub.subscription_id = r.subscription_id) as refunded_revenue,
        uniqExactIf(sub.subscription_id || sub.product_code, sub.subscription_id = c.subscription_id and sub.subscription_id = ch.subscription_id and dateDiff('day', charged_dt, canceled_dt) between 0 and 14) as cancels
    from subscribed as sub
    left join charged as ch
        on sub.subscription_id = ch.subscription_id
        and sub.product_code = ch.product_code
    left join refunded as r
        on sub.subscription_id = r.subscription_id
        and sub.product_code = r.product_code
    left join canceled as c
        on sub.subscription_id = c.subscription_id
        and sub.product_code = c.product_code
    group by 1, 2
)
select
    u.variation as variation,
    uniqExact(u.unified_id) as members,
    uniqExactIf(u.unified_id, u.unified_id = sub.unified_id and sub.accesses > 0) as subscribed,
    uniqExactIf(u.unified_id, u.unified_id = sub.unified_id and sub.charged_revenue > 0) as charged,
    sumIf(sub.charged_revenue, u.unified_id = sub.unified_id and sub.charged_revenue > 0) as charged_revenue,
    uniqExactIf(u.unified_id, u.unified_id = sub.unified_id and sub.refunded_revenue > 0) as refunded,
    sumIf(sub.refunded_revenue, u.unified_id = sub.unified_id and sub.refunded_revenue > 0) as refunded_revenue,
    charged_revenue - refunded_revenue as final_revenue,
    uniqExactIf(u.unified_id, u.unified_id = sub.unified_id and sub.cancels > 0) as canceled,
    
    sumIf(sub.accesses, u.unified_id = sub.unified_id and sub.accesses > 0) as accesses,
    sumIf(sub.accesses, u.unified_id = sub.unified_id and sub.accesses > 0 and is_trial > 0) as accesses_trial,
    sumIf(sub.accesses, u.unified_id = sub.unified_id and sub.accesses > 0 and is_trial = 0) as accesses_instant,
    sumIf(sub.charges, u.unified_id = sub.unified_id and sub.charges > 0) as charges,
    sumIf(sub.charges, u.unified_id = sub.unified_id and sub.charges > 0 and is_trial > 0) as charges_trial,
    sumIf(sub.charges, u.unified_id = sub.unified_id and sub.charges > 0 and is_trial = 0) as charges_instant,
    sumIf(sub.refunds, u.unified_id = sub.unified_id and sub.refunds > 0) as refunds,
    sumIf(sub.cancels, u.unified_id = sub.unified_id and sub.cancels > 0) as cancels,
    
    stddevSamp(sub.charged_revenue - sub.refunded_revenue) as arpu_std,
    stddevSampIf(sub.charged_revenue - sub.refunded_revenue, sub.accesses>0) as arppu_std,
    stddevSampIf((sub.charged_revenue - sub.refunded_revenue) / sub.accesses, sub.accesses>0) as aov_std
from exp_users u
left join sub sub
    on u.unified_id = sub.unified_id
group by 1

with exp_data as (
    select distinct
        id, name,
        toDateTime(date_start) as datetime_start,
        toDateTime(date_end) as datetime_end
    from default.ab_experiments as e
    where id = 7328
        and name like '%[UG Monetization]%'
)
, exp_users as (
    select 
        experiments.variation[indexOf(rt.experiments.id, 7328)] as variation,
        rt.unified_id as unified_id,
        argMin(user_id > 0, datetime) AS is_auth,
        min(rt.datetime) as exp_start_datetime,
        min(e.datetime_end) as exp_end_datetime
    from default.ug_rt_events_web rt
    left join exp_data e 
        on rt.item_id = e.id
    where rt.date between '2026-05-04' and '2026-05-11'
        and rt.event in ('App Experiment Start')
        and has(rt.experiments.id, 7328)
        and rt.item_id = 7328
        and rt.unified_id <> 0
        and rt.platform = 1
        and rt.datetime between e.datetime_start and if(toDate(e.datetime_end) = '1970-01-01', toDateTime('2029-01-01'), e.datetime_end)
    group by 1, 2
)
, subscribed as (
    select
        s.subscription_id as subscription_id,
        s.product_code as product_code,
        e.variation as variation,
        s.base_price,
        product_id,
        max(s.unified_id) as unified_id,
        min(s.datetime) as subscribed_dt,
        min(s.date) as subscribed_date
    from default.ug_subscriptions_events s
    inner join exp_users e
        on s.unified_id = e.unified_id
    where s.date between '2026-05-04' and '2026-05-11'
        and s.platform like '%WEB%'
        and s.event = 'Subscribed'
        and s.datetime between e.exp_start_datetime and if(toDate(e.exp_end_datetime) = '1970-01-01', toDateTime('2029-01-01'), e.exp_end_datetime)
        and lower(funnel_source) not like '%email%'
    group by 1, 2, 3, 4, 5
)
, charged as (
    select
        subscription_id,
        product_code,
        min(case
            when product_id = 'com.ultimateguitar.tabs.one.intro.1year2' then 39.99
            when product_id like '%.intro.%' and billing_cycle = 1 then usd_price * 0.5
            else usd_price
        end) as charged_revenue,
        min(datetime) as charged_dt
    from default.ug_subscriptions_events
    where date >= '2026-05-04'
        and platform like '%WEB%'
        and event = 'Charged'
    group by 1, 2
)
, refunded as (
    select
        subscription_id,
        product_code,
        min(case
            when product_id = 'com.ultimateguitar.tabs.one.intro.1year2' then 39.99
            when product_id like '%.intro.%' and billing_cycle = 1 then usd_price * 0.5
            else usd_price
        end) as refunded_revenue,
        min(datetime) as refunded_dt
    from default.ug_subscriptions_events
    where date >= '2026-05-04'
        and platform like '%WEB%'
        and event = 'Refunded'
    group by 1, 2
)
, canceled as (
    select
        subscription_id,
        product_code,
        min(datetime) as canceled_dt
    from default.ug_subscriptions_events
    where date >= '2026-05-04'
        and platform like '%WEB%'
        and event = 'Canceled'
    group by 1, 2
)
select
    product_id,
    sub.variation as variation,
    uniqExact(sub.unified_id||sub.subscription_id) as accesses,
    uniqExactIf(sub.unified_id||sub.subscription_id, sub.product_code = ch.product_code) as charges,
    uniqExactIf(sub.unified_id||sub.subscription_id, sub.product_code = ch.product_code and sub.product_code = c.product_code) as cancels,
    cancels / charges * 100,
    uniqExactIf(sub.unified_id||sub.subscription_id, sub.product_code = r.product_code) as refunds,
    sumIf(ch.charged_revenue, sub.subscription_id = ch.subscription_id) as charged_revenue,
    sumIf(r.refunded_revenue, sub.subscription_id = r.subscription_id) as refunded_revenue,
    charged_revenue - refunded_revenue as final_revenue
from subscribed as sub
left join charged as ch
    on sub.subscription_id = ch.subscription_id
    and sub.product_code = ch.product_code
left join refunded as r
    on sub.subscription_id = r.subscription_id
    and sub.product_code = r.product_code
left join canceled as c
    on sub.subscription_id = c.subscription_id
    and sub.product_code = c.product_code
group by 1, 2
order by 1, 2
